title: Translate a session imported from Claude Code into a Codex 0.156.0 rollout with a loss account beside it
blocked_by: R10 and R11 only: a Codex account that can make requests, logged into a scratch Codex home by the person running the proof with Codex's own login act; every row before them lands on its own evidence without it.
purpose: The home's first translation to another harness, one named pair and one measured version: a session imported from Claude Code is rendered as a rollout in the shape Codex 0.156.0 writes and reads for its own threads, with every text part, tool call and tool result carried whole as Codex's own items, readable thinking carried as text and opaque blocks dropped (P3), and a JSON loss account beside it naming by entry id and hash what was kept, what changed and how, and what was lost and why. It improves on Codex's own importer of Claude Code files, which is a compaction and not a copy, and never adopts or calls it (ADR-019). The Codex thread is a fork of the session, never the same session: it announces itself in band, and its durable link back is the loss account and a side leaf on the session, which a Codex compaction cannot erase.
task: Add a Codex profile beside the Claude Code one, crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/, and a subcommand `lys-home translate-codex --home H --session S --out DIR --codex-version V --zone Z` in its own crates/lys-home/src/cli_translate.rs (cli.rs is 433 code lines against the 500-line cap, so it gains only the variant and its dispatch). `--out` is a Codex home directory: the rollout is written under it at Codex's own layout, sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<local date and time>-<thread id>.jsonl, and the loss account beside it. The render walks the session's context path as the Claude Code render does (entry order, then part order), reads no clock, no random source and no network, and derives the thread id as record_uuid of the session head (ADR-016, CN9), so each head makes a new Codex thread. **The Codex thread is a fork of the session and not the same session:** once Codex continues it, its turns never come home. The in-band marker says so, but a Codex compaction can erase it, so the durable link back is the loss account and the lys.translation side leaf the translation hangs beside the context path (ADR-012), which never moves the head, so the Claude Code render of the same session is unchanged by a byte. The item shape is the one measured from rollouts Codex writes on the machine the proof runs on; rollouts written by 0.155 on that machine are the starting point for the tool items, because the only 0.156.0 rollout there holds no tool item, and R10's recording is what decides: if it shows a shape R3 or R4 did not write, R10 corrects the render and every earlier test is run again. Codex's source checkout on the proving machine, older than 0.156.0, is never read as the shape. The Codex account: this brief names none of its own and never uses an account that sits at its usage limit; R10 and R11 run in a scratch Codex home, never the live one, with the login the person running the proof makes there by `codex login`; no step copies auth.json or any credential file (CN8, ADR-001). R10's recording and R11's resume are the last two rows and are the only ones that spend Codex requests; everything before them lands on its own evidence. The marker carries no template hash: no Codex launch template exists and none takes part, so the marker names the source session id, the source head hash (Session::head_hash at render time) and the Codex version the rollout shape was recorded against, the same three things the account and the side leaf carry, so all three name one thing. The account measures the entry as the home holds it: a part's hash is the SHA-256 of the part's bytes as the entry holds it, the rule the Claude Code render's loss account already uses, and kept means the Codex item carries that part whole. What the importer lost at import time (a tool_use's caller field, a thinking part's renamed keys) is the importer's loss and belongs to the importer's own account, not to this translation's; the translation never reads a stored block and has no BlockNotStored refusal. A field the entry's part itself holds beyond what its Codex item carries is still counted as changed. An image part whose source is base64 is carried as Codex's input_image item with no `detail` key, in a user message and inside a tool result alike, and R11 measures that Codex 0.156.0 resumes a thread holding one; an image of any other source is listed lost and never fetched, and the translation reads nothing beyond the session file. Out of scope: Codex to Claude Code; adopting, wrapping or calling Codex's importer; Pi or any third harness; launching Codex through the launch template; Codex's thread index (state_5.sqlite, session_index.jsonl), which the render never writes; and any change to the Claude Code render or the importer.

requirements.title: Refuse an unmeasured Codex version, an unnamed or unknown time zone, an existing target and an unparsed stamp, each naming the act that answers it
requirements.spec: Add crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/ (mod.rs holding only `pub mod` lines and `#[cfg(test)] mod` lines) and declare it in harness/mod.rs. In harness/codex/zone.rs define the measured version `0.156.0` and two checks. WHEN the Codex version given is not exactly `0.156.0`, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnmeasuredCodexVersion, whose message is `Codex <version> has no measured rollout shape: render for 0.156.0 or card a measurement of the new version`. IF the zone given is absent, empty, or not an IANA-shaped name (one or more components of ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `+` and `-`, joined by single `/`, with no leading `/` or `:`), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnnamedTimeZone, whose message is `TZ <value> is not an IANA time zone name: set TZ to an IANA name`, with `<value>` the word `unset` when absent. IF the zone is IANA-shaped and not in the time zone database, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::UnknownTimeZone, whose message is `time zone <zone> is not in the time zone database: set TZ to an IANA name`. The zone resolves through the jiff crate with its bundled time zone database, added as a workspace dependency, so one zone name gives the same offsets on every machine. Add two variants for the translation's own refusals, beside LaunchTargetExists: HomeError::TranslationTargetExists, whose message is `translate-codex target already exists: <path>; choose another --out`, and HomeError::StampNotRfc3339, whose message is `entry <entry id> has a stamp that is not RFC 3339: re-import the source file`. HomeError::Exists, which import, canon, the Claude Code render, fewshot and the seed also raise, is left as it is; no existing variant's message changes. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT read an environment variable in harness/codex/, SHALL NOT fall back to UTC or the machine's zone, SHALL NOT accept a version by prefix, and SHALL NOT write any file before each check has passed.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::version_other_than_measured_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the check of `0.157.0` displays exactly `Codex 0.157.0 has no measured rollout shape: render for 0.156.0 or card a measurement of the new version`, the check of `0.156` is refused with the same variant, and the check of `0.156.0` passes.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::unnamed_zone_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts an absent zone displays exactly `TZ unset is not an IANA time zone name: set TZ to an IANA name`, and that `` (empty) and `:/etc/localtime` are each refused as UnnamedTimeZone.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::unknown_zone_is_refused` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts `Mars/Olympus` displays exactly `time zone Mars/Olympus is not in the time zone database: set TZ to an IANA name`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::named_zone_resolves` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the instant `2026-09-23T02:14:53.850Z` in zone `Australia/Sydney` is local `2026-09-23T12:14:53`, and that `UTC` resolves.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::zone_tests::translation_refusals_name_the_act` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts HomeError::TranslationTargetExists with path `a/b.jsonl` displays exactly `translate-codex target already exists: a/b.jsonl; choose another --out`, HomeError::StampNotRfc3339 with entry id `e1` displays exactly `entry e1 has a stamp that is not RFC 3339: re-import the source file`, and HomeError::Exists with path `a/b.jsonl` still displays exactly `session file already exists: a/b.jsonl`.
`grep -rn 'std::env' crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/` prints nothing.

requirements.title: Define the loss account: kept, changed and lost rows by entry id and hash, and nothing of the content
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/account.rs define the account written beside a rollout: a JSON object with exactly the keys `session` (the home session's id), `head` (the head entry's id), `head_hash` (Session::head_hash of the session at translation time, the source head hash the marker names), `thread` (the Codex thread id), `codex_version`, `kept`, `changed` and `lost`. A kept row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `before` and `after`; a changed row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `before`, `after` and `how`, where `how` names every field that was not carried or was reshaped, joined by `; `; a lost row has exactly `entry`, `hash`, `kind` and `reason`. `hash` is the SHA-256, lowercase hex, of serde_json::to_vec of the part (or of the tool-result message) as the home entry holds it, the rule the Claude Code render's loss account uses, and is null for a row about an entry rather than a part. Rows are in walk order. The account measures the entry as the home holds it; what the importer lost when the source file was imported is the importer's loss, recorded by the importer's own account and not by this one. The account is written with create_new and synced before the translation reports. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write into the account any text, argument, output, summary, note, epilogue or seed, only ids, hashes, kind names, field names and the fixed reason words this brief gives, and SHALL NOT count a part as kept when any of its fields was not carried or was reshaped.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::account_tests::account_holds_the_three_lists` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test builds an account with one row of each list and asserts its top-level keys are exactly `changed, codex_version, head, head_hash, kept, lost, session, thread`, a kept row's keys exactly `after, before, entry, hash`, a changed row's exactly `after, before, entry, hash, how`, a lost row's exactly `entry, hash, kind, reason`, and a row about an entry has `hash` null.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::account_tests::part_hash_is_the_entry_bytes` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the test asserts the hash of the part `{"type":"text","text":"a"}` is `a7be9c132fa673d4eb9460cf2601c67404000175f92f2a576610aec68877d516` (computed independently by `printf '%s' '{"text":"a","type":"text"}' | shasum -a 256`).

requirements.title: Carry each part whole as Codex's own item, thinking as text and base64 images as input_image, and count what changed
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/parts.rs map one message entry to Codex 0.156.0 response items and account rows. A user message's text parts, and string content, become one `message` item with role `user` and one `input_text` part per text, each text copied byte for byte; each is kept, before `text`, after `input_text`. An assistant message becomes items in part order: consecutive text and readable thinking parts form one `message` item with role `assistant` and one `output_text` part each; a toolCall part becomes one `function_call` item with `name`, `call_id` equal to the part's own id, and `arguments` equal to serde_json::to_string of the part's arguments, whole; a text part is kept, before `text`, after `output_text`; a toolCall is kept, before `toolCall`, after `function_call`. Every thinking part is treated as another provider's (the translation names no target model and the home's imported thinking is Anthropic's): readable thinking becomes an `output_text` part and is changed, before `thinking`, after `output_text`, with how `thinkingSignature not carried` when the part holds a signature and `thinking written as output_text` otherwise; redacted thinking is lost, reason `redacted thinking dropped: another provider`; thinking with no readable text is lost, reason `empty thinking dropped`. A toolResult entry becomes one `function_call_output` item with `call_id` equal to its toolCallId and `output` equal to its one text part's text as a string when its content is exactly one text part (how `content: one-item text array written as a string`), otherwise a list holding, in content order, `{"type":"input_text","text":…}` for each text part and the input_image item below for each base64 image part; it is one changed row keyed by the entry id and the hash of the toolResult message, before `toolResult`, after `function_call_output`, whose how also names `isError not carried`, `timestamp not carried` and `toolName not carried` for each of those keys the message holds. An image part (`{"type":"image","source":{…}}`, as the entry holds it in a user message or a tool result's content) whose source type is `base64` becomes `{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:<media_type>;base64,<data>"}` with `<data>` copied byte for byte and no `detail` key, since the Claude session never held one (R11 measures that Codex 0.156.0 resumes a thread holding such an item, and if it does not, R11 adds the key as its conditional says), in its place among the message's parts or the output list, and is changed, before `image`, after `input_image`, how `source written as a data URL image_url`. An image part whose source type is anything else is left out and is a lost row with the part's hash, kind `image` and reason `image source <source type> not carried: part <index>, never fetched`, where `<index>` is the part's 0-based position in the content array that holds it; no byte of the source's value is written anywhere. A part of any other kind (an unknown assistant kind, a document) is lost, reason `Codex has no item for kind <kind> in this render`. A part holding a field beyond those its item carries (text: type, text; toolCall: type, id, name, arguments; thinking: type, thinking, thinkingSignature, redacted), a caller field included, is changed instead of kept, how naming `<field> not carried` for each. Each user and assistant message entry whose message holds a key other than role and content gets one changed row with hash null, before `<role> message`, after `message item`, how naming `<key> not carried` for each such key in sorted order, so an assistant turn's model, usage and stop reason are named. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT clip or summarise any text, argument or output, SHALL NOT write an `[external_agent_tool_call` or `[external_agent_tool_result` note, SHALL NOT write a `custom_tool_call`, a `reasoning` item or `encrypted_content`, SHALL NOT write a thinking signature or redacted data into an item, and SHALL NOT write an `id` key on any item, SHALL NOT write a `detail` key on an input_image item, and SHALL NOT fetch a URL or read any file to carry an image.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::tool_call_becomes_function_call` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a toolCall `{"type":"toolCall","id":"toolu_1","name":"Bash","arguments":{"command":"ls"}}` gives exactly `{"type":"function_call","name":"Bash","arguments":"{\"command\":\"ls\"}","call_id":"toolu_1"}` and one kept row before `toolCall`, after `function_call`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::caller_field_is_changed` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; the same toolCall with `"caller":{"type":"direct"}` added gives the same item and one changed row with how exactly `caller not carried` and no kept row.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::one_item_result_is_a_string` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a toolResult message with toolCallId `toolu_1`, toolName `Bash`, content `[{"type":"text","text":"ok"}]`, isError false and timestamp 1 gives exactly `{"type":"function_call_output","call_id":"toolu_1","output":"ok"}` and one changed row with how exactly `content: one-item text array written as a string; isError not carried; timestamp not carried; toolName not carried`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::two_item_result_is_a_list` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; content with text parts `a` then `b` gives `output` exactly `[{"type":"input_text","text":"a"},{"type":"input_text","text":"b"}]`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::assistant_turn_fields_are_named` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; an assistant message with keys role, content, api, provider, model, usage, stopReason and timestamp gives one row with hash null and how exactly `api not carried; model not carried; provider not carried; stopReason not carried; timestamp not carried; usage not carried`, and that row is in `changed`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::thinking_is_text_and_opaque_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a thinking part with thinking `t` and thinkingSignature `sig` gives an `output_text` part with text `t` and a changed row with how `thinkingSignature not carried`; a redacted thinking part gives no item and a lost row whose hash is the part's hash and whose reason is exactly `redacted thinking dropped: another provider`; the serialised items contain neither `sig` nor `encrypted_content`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::parts_tests::base64_image_is_input_image_and_url_image_is_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a user message whose content is a text part `look`, an image part with source `{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":"iVBORw0KGgo="}` and an image part with source `{"type":"url","url":"https://example.invalid/a.png"}` gives one `message` item whose content is exactly `[{"type":"input_text","text":"look"},{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo="}]`, one changed row before `image`, after `input_image`, and one lost row with kind `image` and reason exactly `image source url not carried: part 2, never fetched`; the serialised items and account contain no `example.invalid`; a toolResult whose content is a text part `shot` and the same base64 image gives `output` exactly `[{"type":"input_text","text":"shot"},{"type":"input_image","image_url":"data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo="}]`.
`grep -rnE 'custom_tool_call|encrypted_content|external_agent|truncat|reqwest|ureq|TcpStream' crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/parts.rs` prints nothing.

requirements.title: Walk the context path and write the rollout at Codex's own layout, opening with the marker
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/rollout.rs, WHEN a session is translated with an out directory, the Codex version and a zone, THE SYSTEM SHALL run R1's checks, then walk session.context_path() and write one rollout at `<out>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-<thread>.jsonl` and its account at the same path with `.jsonl` replaced by `.loss.json`, where `<thread>` is record_uuid(session id, head entry id) and the date and time are the head entry's own stamp in the given zone, seconds truncated. IF either path exists, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::TranslationTargetExists naming it and write nothing. Every entry's stamp on the context path is parsed as RFC 3339 before any file is written; IF one does not parse, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with HomeError::StampNotRfc3339 naming that entry's id, and write nothing. Every line is `{"timestamp","ordinal","type","payload"}` with `ordinal` the 0-based line number. Line 0 is `session_meta` whose payload holds exactly `id` and `session_id` (both the thread id), `timestamp` (the head entry's stamp as recorded), `cwd` (the session header's cwd) and `cli_version` (the Codex version given). Line 1 is a `response_item` `message` with role `developer` and one `input_text` part holding exactly the marker `<TRANSLATED CONTEXT: THIS CODEX THREAD IS A FORK OF HOME SESSION {session id} AT HEAD HASH {source head hash}, RENDERED FOR CODEX {codex version}, NOT THAT SESSION>`, where the source head hash is Session::head_hash at translation time and the Codex version is the one given; the marker carries no template hash, since no launch template takes part. Then each context-path entry in order: message entries through R3, with each line's `timestamp` the entry's own stamp; a compaction entry as one `developer` message whose text is `<COMPACTION SUMMARY <entry id>>`, a newline and the summary whole, counted changed with hash null, before `compaction`, after `marked text`; every other entry on the path (a custom entry, a label, a model change, a branch summary) as a lost row with hash null, `kind` its customType or its type, and reason `Codex has no item for it and it is not conversation`. The rollout is written with create_new and synced, then the account. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write model_provider, source, thread_source, history_mode, originator, base_instructions or any other key into session_meta; SHALL NOT write a turn_context, event_msg or any line kind other than session_meta and response_item; SHALL NOT read a clock or a random source; SHALL NOT write outside `<out>`; and SHALL NOT write Codex's thread index. IF R11 measures that Codex 0.156.0 cannot resume without one of those keys or line kinds, THEN R11 adds exactly that one and the account names it as a changed entry-level line with hash null, before `none` and after the key or line kind.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::path_follows_codex_layout` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a session with id `s1` whose head entry `11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` is stamped `2026-09-23T02:14:53.850Z`, translated with zone `Australia/Sydney` into out `o`, writes `o/sessions/2026/09/23/rollout-2026-09-23T12-14-53-11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111.jsonl` and `o/sessions/2026/09/23/rollout-2026-09-23T12-14-53-11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111.loss.json`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::session_meta_holds_five_keys` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; line 0's payload keys are exactly `cli_version, cwd, id, session_id, timestamp`, and `grep -cE 'model_provider|thread_source|history_mode|originator'` on the rollout prints `0`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::marker_opens_the_thread` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; line 1 is a `developer` message whose one `input_text` part is exactly `<TRANSLATED CONTEXT: THIS CODEX THREAD IS A FORK OF HOME SESSION s1 AT HEAD HASH <h>, RENDERED FOR CODEX 0.156.0, NOT THAT SESSION>` with `<h>` the session's Session::head_hash, and the account's `session`, `head_hash` and `codex_version` equal `s1`, `<h>` and `0.156.0`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::thread_id_is_record_uuid_of_head` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; for a head entry id `h-r0` in session `s1` the thread id in the file name and in session_meta equals record_uuid(`s1`, `h-r0`), a string with version nibble 5.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::ordinal_is_the_line_number` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; every line's `ordinal` equals its 0-based line number, and every line's `type` is `session_meta` or `response_item`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::compaction_is_marked_text` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a compaction entry on the path gives one developer message whose text begins `<COMPACTION SUMMARY ` followed by the entry id, and one changed row before `compaction`, after `marked text`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::rollout_tests::unparsed_stamp_is_refused_and_nothing_written` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a session whose second context-path entry `e2` is stamped `yesterday` fails with exactly `entry e2 has a stamp that is not RFC 3339: re-import the source file`, and `--out` holds no file afterwards.
`grep -rnE 'fresh_id|rand::|now\(|SystemTime|Instant|std::env' crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex/rollout.rs` prints nothing.

requirements.title: Carry labelled sidechains as marked text and a forked child's point as the first prompt, and list every other entry off the path, lys entries and unlabelled branches among them, as lost
requirements.spec: In harness/codex/beside.rs, for each label entry off the context path whose label begins `agent ` and whose parent is on the path, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry the sidechain it names (the label's target entry and the message entries descending from it, through any custom entry between them, in file order) as one `developer` message placed directly after the items of the label's parent entry, whose text is the line `<SIDECHAIN <target id> UNDER ENTRY <parent id>>`, then for each of its message entries a line `[<role> <entry id>]` followed by its parts as lines: a text part and readable thinking whole, a toolCall as `[tool call <id> <name>] ` and its arguments as compact JSON, a toolResult as `[tool result <toolCallId>]` and then each of its text parts whole. Each sidechain message entry is one changed row with hash null, before `sidechain`, after `marked text`, how `carried as marked text under entry <parent id>`; an opaque thinking part or a non-text part inside it is left out and is a lost row as in R3. Each custom entry off the path that descends from an entry on the path is a lost row with hash null, `kind` its customType and reason `Codex has no item for it and it is not conversation`, wherever it hangs: directly under the path, under another such custom entry, inside a carried sidechain (the tool_completed event the importer hangs under each sidechain tool result, and each attachment or system event the importer places on the sidechain's own chain), or inside an unlabelled branch; this includes every harness event, lantern, epilogue and lys.given entry, and any lys custom type added later. A sidechain whose first Claude Code record has no agentId is imported under the path with no label, and the home record keeps no flag that tells it from any other branch off the path, so it is listed and not carried: each message entry off the path that descends from an entry on the path and is not in a carried sidechain is a lost row with its entry id, hash null, `kind` `unlabelled branch` and reason `off the context path with no agent label: not carried`. WHEN the session is a child forked at a user message (ADR-018), THE SYSTEM SHALL write the carried message's text, read through the same seed_of the Claude Code render uses, as one `user` message directly after the marker, so it is the rollout's first user item, and count it as changed with the point's entry id, hash null, before `point`, after `first prompt`. Its tests import synthetic Claude Code files through lys_home::cli::run into a temporary home. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT drop a sidechain, SHALL NOT leave a custom entry or a message entry off the path out of the account, SHALL NOT carry an entry of an unlabelled branch off the path, and SHALL NOT write the seed's text into the account or the report.
acceptance: `cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::beside_tests::sidechain_is_carried_as_marked_text` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a Claude Code fixture whose main chain is a user and an assistant record, followed by two sidechain records with agentId `a1`, gives one developer item whose first line is `<SIDECHAIN <first sidechain uuid> UNDER ENTRY <assistant uuid>>`, which contains each sidechain text part whole, which is the next item after the assistant's items, and exactly 2 changed rows with before `sidechain` and after `marked text`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::beside_tests::lys_entries_are_listed_lost` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; after `lys-home lantern light` at the fixture's head and an imported `attachment` record, the account holds a lost row whose entry is the lantern's id with kind `lys.lantern` and reason exactly `Codex has no item for it and it is not conversation`, and a lost row with kind `lys.harness_event`.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::beside_tests::sidechain_descendants_and_unlabelled_branch_are_listed` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a Claude Code fixture whose main chain is a user and an assistant record, followed by a sidechain with agentId `a1` holding an assistant record with one tool_use, a user record with its tool_result and an `attachment` record parented on that user record, and then a sidechain of one user and one assistant record whose first record has no agentId, gives an account holding exactly 2 lost rows of kind `lys.harness_event` whose entries are off the path under the `a1` sidechain (its tool_completed event and its attachment), exactly 2 lost rows of kind `unlabelled branch` with reason exactly `off the context path with no agent label: not carried`, one per message entry of the unlabelled sidechain, and no rollout item containing that sidechain's text.

`cargo test -p lys-home --lib -- --exact harness::codex::beside_tests::forked_child_opens_on_the_point` prints `1 passed; 0 failed`; a lantern lit at a user message and forked through `lys-home fork` gives a child whose rollout's first item with role `user` has one `input_text` part equal to that message's text, and whose account has a changed row with the point's entry id, before `point`, after `first prompt`.

requirements.title: Record each translation as a lys.translation side leaf that never moves the head
requirements.spec: Add the custom type `lys.translation` to record/entries.rs beside the other lys custom types. In harness/codex/leaf.rs, WHEN the rollout and the account are both written and synced, THE SYSTEM SHALL append one lys.translation custom entry beside the context path through Session::append_beside, whose data holds exactly `harness` (`codex`), `codex_version`, `thread`, `head` (the head entry's id), `head_hash` (Session::head_hash before the append), `rollout` (the rollout's path relative to `--out`), `rollout_sha256` and `account_sha256`. Being a custom entry off the path whose parent is on it, the leaf falls under R5's rule, so a second translation of the same head lists the first translation's side leaf as lost. This leaf and the account are the durable link from the Codex fork back to the session. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT move the head, SHALL NOT change an earlier byte of the session file, SHALL NOT write an absolute path or any content into the data, and SHALL NOT append the leaf when a write before it failed.

requirements.title: Add the translate-codex subcommand and its report of paths and counts

WHEN it succeeds, THE SYSTEM SHALL print one JSON object `{"command": "translate-codex", "report": …}` whose report holds exactly `rollout` (the rollout's path), `account` (the account's path), `entries` (entries walked on the context path), `blocks` (content parts walked), `kept`, `changed` and `lost` (the row counts of the account). IF any refusal fires, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit 1 with the refusal's message on stderr and nothing on stdout, and write nothing. cli.rs gains only the variant and its dispatch; lib.rs declares the module and its sibling test file. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT print any text, argument, output, summary or seed, and SHALL NOT run Codex (ADR-007).

requirements.title: Record a Codex 0.156.0 rollout in a scratch Codex home and match the fixture session's render to it
requirements.spec: Prerequisite, done once by the person running the proof: a scratch Codex home directory, never the live one, into which that person has logged a Codex account with `CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex login`; no file is copied into it. At its start the recording checks, with CODEX_HOME set to the scratch home: IF `codex login status` exits non-zero, THEN it stops, records `Refused: the scratch Codex home holds no login; run codex login with CODEX_HOME set to it`, and writes no fixture; IF one small request (`codex exec` asking for one word) fails because the account is at its usage limit, THEN it stops, records `Refused: the account cannot make requests until <the reset date Codex reports>; log an account that can make requests into the scratch home, or wait for that date`, and writes no fixture. Then, with TZ set to an IANA name, it records at most 3 times one `codex exec` exchange in which Codex runs one shell command and answers; the first recording whose rollout holds a `function_call` and its `function_call_output` is kept, and IF none of 3 does, THEN it stops and records `Refused: no function_call in 3 recordings`. From the kept recording commit crates/lys-home/tests/fixtures/codex/rollout-0.156.0.jsonl, the recording's `response_item` lines of type `function_call`, `function_call_output`, and `message` with role `assistant` or with role `user` whose text is the prompt, in recorded order and otherwise as Codex wrote them, and crates/lys-home/tests/fixtures/codex/claude_code.jsonl, a Claude Code file mirroring those items (the prompt as the user text, each tool call's name and parsed arguments as a tool_use, each output as its tool_result, each assistant text as an assistant text); an absolute path of the recording machine in either file is replaced by `/fixture` in both, and the count replaced is recorded. WHEN claude_code.jsonl is imported and translated, THE SYSTEM SHALL write response items after the marker whose payloads equal the fixture rollout's payloads in order apart from the keys `id`, `call_id` and `internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough`. IF they differ in any other key or value, THEN R3 or R4 is corrected to write what Codex wrote, a key whose value the Claude session never held is named in the account as changed with before `none` and after the key, and every test of R1 to R8 is run again. docs/design/home/PROOF-TRANSLATE.md is created with a recording section whose lines are `Recording codex version: `, `Recording login status exit: `, `Recording start check exit: `, `Recording TZ: `, `Recording attempts: `, `Paths replaced by /fixture: `, `Fixture rollout SHA-256: ` and `Recording live Codex home rollouts before and after: `, each once; R11 adds the resume section's own lines. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT use the live Codex home, SHALL NOT copy an auth file, SHALL NOT record more than 3 times, and SHALL NOT record any transcript content, account email or credential value in the proof.

requirements.title: Resume the rendered thread, and a thread holding an image, on Codex 0.156.0 in the scratch home and record it with hashes, counts and paths only
requirements.spec: With the same scratch Codex home, the same start check as R10 and its refusal words, and TZ set to an IANA name: import tests/fixtures/codex/claude_code.jsonl into a fresh home, translate it with `lys-home translate-codex --out <scratch> --codex-version 0.156.0`, take the rollout's SHA-256 and read the lys.translation side leaf's `rollout_sha256` from the session, both after the translation and before any resume, and then resume the thread with `CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex exec resume <thread id> <question>`, where the question can be answered only from a token the fixture's tool result holds. Because the resume writes to the thread's rollout, its SHA-256 is taken again after the resume and recorded on its own line. Then import tests/fixtures/codex/claude_code_image.jsonl, a synthetic Claude Code file created by this requirement whose one user record holds a text part and a base64 PNG image part the proof generates (no photograph, screenshot or transcript), translate it into the same scratch home, count the rollout's `input_image` items and those among them holding a `detail` key, and resume that thread with one question asking for one word. Before that resume, run `CODEX_HOME=<scratch> codex exec --image <the same PNG> <one question asking for one word>` once, so that Codex 0.156.0 writes an image-bearing rollout of its own in the scratch home, and read the `detail` value of its input_image item. WHEN Codex 0.156.0 answers, THE SYSTEM SHALL have the proof record a resume section of these lines, each once: `Resume codex version: ` (the `codex --version` output); `Account: ` (the label the person running the proof gives it, never an email or credential); `Resume login status exit: `; `Resume start check exit: `; `Resume TZ: `; `Rollout path: ` and `Account path: ` (relative to the scratch home, the report's `rollout` and `account`); `Rollout SHA-256: ` (after translation, before the resume); `Side leaf rollout_sha256: `; `Rollout SHA-256 after resume: `; `Account SHA-256: `; `Thread id: `; `Counts: entries <n> blocks <n> kept <n> changed <n> lost <n>` from the report; `Resume exit: `; `Answer token matches: ` (the count of the token in the answer); `Head hash before: ` and `Head hash after: `; `Image input_image items: `; `Image input_image items with detail: `; `Detail measured from: <rollout path relative to the scratch home> <value>` (the rollout Codex wrote for the `--image` run and the `detail` value on its input_image item); `Image resume exit: `; and `Resume live Codex home rollouts before and after: `. IF a resume fails because a key or line kind R4 left out is needed, or the image resume fails because an input_image lacks `detail`, THEN that one key or line kind is added once (for `detail`, the value recorded on the `Detail measured from: ` line, never a value read from another version's rollouts or assumed, named in the account as changed with before `none` and after `detail <value>`), the failure's exit status and the added key are recorded on a line `Added after failed resume: <exit> <key>`, and the translations and both resumes are run again. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT resume in the live Codex home, SHALL NOT write Codex's thread index by hand, and SHALL NOT record the question, the answer, the image or any transcript text.

boundaries: No change to the Claude Code render (harness/claude_code/render.rs), the importer (import.rs), seed.rs or the bytes any of them write; the translation reuses record_uuid and seed_of as they are.
No call, wrapper or port of Codex's importer of Claude Code files, and no shape read from Codex's source checkout.
No harness other than Claude Code to Codex, no Codex to Claude Code, no Pi, and no launch of Codex through the launch template or otherwise; the subcommand never runs Codex.
No write into the live Codex home, Codex's state_5.sqlite, thread_history_1.sqlite or session_index.jsonl, and no copy of auth.json or any credential file anywhere.
No new role, namespace or name form for derived uuids (ADR-016): the thread id is record_uuid of the head and a call id is the record's own tool id.
No transcript content in the report, the account, an error, a test name, a log line or PROOF-TRANSLATE.md.

No template hash in the marker or the side leaf, no BlockNotStored refusal, and no read of a stored block: the account measures each part as the home entry holds it, and what the importer lost at import time belongs to the importer's own account.
No URL fetched and no file read beyond the home's session file: an image whose source is not base64 is listed lost, never fetched.
No Codex version but 0.156.0, and no more than 3 recordings.
